keyFindings.description: On a nats-server 2.10 cluster (testnats.Image is nats:2.10; Go tests link v2.10.29) a DiscardNew refusal leaves the message id staged with seq 0 (jetstream_cluster.go:7995, not removed on ErrMaxBytes at stream.go:4669-4700), so the retry of a GitHub delivery or Dispatch event (same Nats-Msg-Id) is acked Duplicate with Sequence 0 and never stored: the webhook answers 200 and the outbox marks it published. Reproduced by the deep reviewer on the in-process 2.10.29 cluster; v2.15.1 is not affected. Fix: treat Duplicate && Sequence == 0 as not stored (retryable) in publishJetStream and the async window (async.go:206), with a cluster full-stream retry test; or document a minimum server version.

ownedStream writes cfg.MaxBytes over any deployed limit, so every program's keeper lowers an operator's emergency raise on a full DiscardNew stream within 30 s (tester saw it, test.json), and the stream refuses every publish again until messages age out (up to 72 h); the only remedy is redeploying every program, while Dispatch's sweep gives up after about 30 min. nats.go:931-933 and webhook docs say an operator raise makes room. Fix: never lower a deployed limit (max of deployed and setting, as for replicas; lowering an operator step), or a correct full-stream runbook and corrected comments.

Claims the keeper of the program whose write was lost puts its part back; false for a start's replacement of an overlapping subject, which keptSubjects skips, so it stays reverted until that program's next start. Name the exception.
keptSubjects' role-lane check on own subjects can never fire (stream_config_test.go fails the build if a compiled subject captures a role lane); drop it, its test row and doc phrases.

Help text hard-codes '1 to 5'; build it from bus.MaxReplicas.
